subject.title: fix(active-memory): recall sub-agent receives huge prompt envelopes; bound recall context to 25K chars

question: Should Active Memory deliberately impose a fixed 25,000-character ceiling on recall context for existing `full` and `recent` configurations, rather than preserve their prior larger-context behavior or introduce an explicit policy boundary?
rationale: The branch fixes a real timeout and cost problem, but it also replaces an established configurable recall-context behavior across all modes; that compatibility tradeoff is product policy rather than a mechanical defect Codex can choose unilaterally.

options.title: Approve the fixed global cap
options.body: Accept bounded recall as the supported behavior for every query mode and add an upgrade-focused test/documented statement that `full` mode retains the request plus newest context only.

options.title: Scope the cap to envelope cases
options.body: Bound only recognized runtime envelopes and leave already-structured non-envelope `full` inputs governed by the existing mode settings.

options.title: Define an explicit operator policy
options.body: Introduce a narrowly justified migration or configuration policy only if maintainers need deployments to choose between strict bounds and wider historical recall.

recommendation.title: Approve the fixed global cap
recommendation.body: Accept bounded recall as the supported behavior for every query mode and add an upgrade-focused test/documented statement that `full` mode retains the request plus newest context only.

likelyOwner.reason: Their earlier focused work and reproduction are the strongest available history signal in the supplied context for the recall-envelope behavior, though current-main ownership should be confirmed by the area owner.
